type: M9-REP PRE-REGISTRATION -- independent replication of H1/H3 on the 91 datasets never touched by any earlier milestone
why_this_is_not_optional_stopping: The primary M9 test (n=38, commit e3f8aca) is COMPLETE and its result STANDS AS REPORTED: H1 p=1.35e-09 supported, H3 rho=+0.227 p=0.086 not significant. We are NOT adding datasets to that test and re-reading its p-value. The 91 datasets here were excluded at M5 by a seeded sample drawn for budget reasons, long before any outcome was seen, and no model has ever been run on them. They therefore form a clean independent sample, and H3-REP below is a FRESH test at its own alpha=0.05. We disclose plainly that this replication was motivated by the primary test being underpowered (3.1x short). The replication-set result is PRIMARY; any pooled estimate is reported as SECONDARY and descriptive only, never as the headline.

hypotheses.H1-REP: TabPFN test log-loss increases under rotation of the numeric block (paired one-sided Wilcoxon, alpha=0.05). Direction fixed by the primary result.
hypotheses.H3-REP: rotation_alignment, computed on the UNROTATED training split, positively predicts the magnitude of TabPFN's degradation (Spearman > 0, one-sided, alpha=0.05). Direction fixed in advance by the primary point estimate (+0.227), so this is a directional confirmatory test.

design: identical to M9 in every respect: same split seed, same rotation rule (Haar-random orthogonal map on the standardized numeric block, train moments only), same >=4-numeric-column eligibility rule, same 1500-row caps, same 16-config tuning budget. Nothing about the procedure changes.

analysis_plan.primary: H1-REP and H3-REP on the replication set ALONE
analysis_plan.secondary: pooled estimate over primary + replication, reported descriptively with both n's stated; no pooled p-value is treated as confirmatory
analysis_plan.no_outcome_dependent_choices: tests, directions and alpha are fixed here
